title: 15+10 · you White · French Winawer
logNote: Saw Nxf5 gxf5 Bxf5 Bxf5 and stopped on my own capture; missed …Qxf5 (ply 5). Clock 12:05 → 3:26 over moves 22–26, then 32.Kg2?? Qg5+.

steps.name: 1 Three ply
steps.title: After 14…Nd6, White to move
steps.prompt: You played 15.Qg3. Name the reply you had to calculate, then write every move until nothing can take back.

mixups.key: That is the game: you saw …Qxf5 at the board, one move too late, and went Bf6 (~−2). The drill is to finish the captures before 15.Qg3, not after.

steps.key: Ply 5 is …Qxf5: the d7 queen through the empty e6. Three attackers, two defenders, a pawn down (~−3). You had ply 1 to 4 in the game. The fifth is the drill.

steps.name: 2 Diagnose
steps.title: After 14…Nd6, White to move
steps.prompt: Count f5 before you move. Count to the last capture, not to the one you like.

questions.name: material
questions.label: 2.1 Material
questions.hint: Who is up, and by how much?

steps.key:
Material: equal. The opening was not the problem: you were better through move 13 (8.O-O and 13.Bg5 let some of it go, nothing more).

f5: three attackers — Nd6, Bg6 and Qd7 — against two defenders, g4 and Bd3. The queen looks through e6, which has been empty since 4.exd5 exd5.

You did not stop at a scary reply this time. You stopped at your own recapture. Ply 5 is …Qxf5.

steps.name: 3 Calculate
steps.title: Four lines from move 15. Count to the end of the captures.
steps.prompt: Open a branch. Play every move, including the one you stopped before. Lock that branch. The step's key opens once all four are locked.

questions.name: whynot
questions.label: After 15.Qg3 Nxf5 gxf5 Bxf5, why not 17.Bxf5?

questions.name: nxd6
questions.label: 15.Nxd6 first — what does it remove from the count?

branches.label: Qg3 Nxf5 gxf5 Bxf5 Bxf5 Qxf5
branches.key: The line you stopped one ply short. You counted the knights off and the bishop taken, then the queen takes back. A pawn down with the kingside open (~−3). Nothing is won.

branches.label: Qg3 Nxf5 gxf5 Bxf5 Bf6 (game)
branches.key: The game. You saw …Qxf5 one move too late and put the bishop on f6 for an attack. After 17…Bg6 18.f4 gxf6 it is still about −2. The attack did not pay for the pawn.

branches.label: Nxd6 Bxd3 cxd3 Qxd6
branches.key: Take the attacker first. The knight is gone, the bishops come off, and nobody is aiming at f5 anymore. About equal.

branches.label: Ne3
branches.key: Engine's first choice, about equal. The knight leaves before it can be counted off and hits d5 from e3. Stepping back is fine when the count is 3 against 2.

steps.key: All four. Qg3 does nothing about f5, and the count loses a pawn. Nxd6 and Ne3 keep it equal. The skill is not seeing Nxf5. You saw it. The skill is playing to the last capture.

steps.name: 4 Clock
steps.title: After 31…Qe3+, White to move (1:42 left)
steps.prompt: Three king moves draw. One loses. Play the game move and the check that punishes it.

branches.label: Kg2 Qg5+ Qxg5 hxg5 (game)
branches.key: …Qg5+ checks down the g-file and hits your queen on d5 along the fifth rank. You have to trade. In the knight-vs-bishop ending g6 falls and Black wins.

branches.label: Kh2 Qf4+ Kh3 Qe3+
branches.key: Off the g-file. Black has only checks, and it is a draw. Kh1 and Kf1 are the same.

steps.key: At 1:42 the question is only: which squares let him check and hit something at the same time? g2 was the only one.

steps.name: 5 Log
steps.title: Tag the loss honestly
steps.prompt: Three moments. Pick the one that cost the game first.

questions.label: 5.2 Moves 22–26 cost nine minutes at about equal. What were you calculating?

steps.key: Tag calculation. Move 15 put you two pawns' worth down, and the clock and Kg2 came after it. Last week you stopped at the reply you disliked (…a6). This week you stopped at the recapture you liked (Bxf5). Same leak. Three more ply.
